answer: Approval requires signers drawn from at least three separate invitation subtrees with no shared inviter within five hops, so one farm branch can occupy only one slot in any approving panel no matter how many identities it registers. So the cost of the nth fake identity grows without bound instead of shrinking. The island is the branch that may occupy one slot, the atlas the five-hop divergence that defines a branch, and the sparrow the panel that counts branches instead of votes; the island and the atlas cap a farm at one seat, and only the sparrow decides the outcome.
